impact: Volunteer (DIVD) email addresses confirmed exfiltrated; signs of partial exfiltration from the GSuite office environment, helpdesk, Jira and Confluence, operational IT systems and the CSIRT ticket system; CSIRT correspondence and zero-day data held in Zammad should be assumed possibly compromised. HR, source code, Slack, accounting and the CVE/CNA environment show no indication of compromise. Investigation ongoing.
mitigations: DIVD blocked datacenter access, formed an incident response team with an external firm, reported the vulnerabilities to Zammad (fixed in 7.2 and 7.2.2), opened a case to warn other Zammad users, notified the Dutch Data Protection Authority and NCSC-NL, and filed a police report on 2026-10-05.
name: DIVD CSIRT ticketing system breached through two Zammad zero-days; AI agents used in later attack stages
summary: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) reports that on 2026-09-21 a malicious actor gained first access to the Zammad instance that serves as its CSIRT ticketing system, using two previously unknown Zammad vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-102489 and CVE-2026-102490, since fixed by Zammad). DIVD detected the intrusion on 2026-09-22 with a stated mean time to detect of 19 minutes, made a first public statement on 2026-09-24 and published its casefile on 2026-09-29. DIVD states that AI agents were used in the later stages of the attack, citing the volume of activity and artifacts generated in a short time and attack scripts that were commented and documented, with the agents appearing to talk to each other in the comments. Volunteer email addresses were confirmed exfiltrated; partial exfiltration is indicated from the office environment, IT and project support systems and CSIRT tickets, which may include correspondence about vulnerable systems. DIVD notified the Dutch data protection authority and NCSC-NL and filed a police report.
